docs.title: ae
docs.text:
This vowel combination occurs exclusively in old Dutch words. You will only find it in proper names, especially in Flanders:

It is pronounced the same way as 'aa' [a] 

meneer Claessen (Mr. Claessen)
mevrouw Haenen (Mrs. Haenen)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ai
docs.text:
This is a rare vowel combination.

Pronounce like English i in wine. [ai]

hai (hi)
mais (corn; also spelled as maïs).
Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: au
docs.text:
Pronounce like the English ou in house [au]

gauw (soon)
grauw (greyish)
lauw (lukewarm)
Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ei
docs.text:
This sound is a bit similar to the German ei in reisen, but pronounced a bit 'flatter' [ɛi] or [æi]

ei (egg)
beleid (policy)
bereiden (to prepare)
geit (goat)
trein (train)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: eu
docs.text:
Pronounce like French 'eu' in 'feu' or German ö in Köln [ø]

leuk (nice, funny)
neus (nose)
heup (hip)
treuzelen (to be slow)
Your browser does not support the audio element.

But: if it precedes the letter r, pronounce like the English or in word [œ]

geur (smell)
kleur (colour)
zeuren (to whine)
deur (door)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ie
docs.text:
Pronounce like ee in the English keep [i]

lief (sweet, dear)
bier (beer)
hier (here)
genieten van (to enjoy)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ij
docs.text:
Same as ei [ɛi] or [æi]

wijs (wise)
blij (happy, glad)
grijs (grey)
tijd (time)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: eo
docs.text:
Pronounce like English oo in choose [u]

voelen (to feel)
goed (good)
zoet (sweet)
voet (foot)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: oi
docs.text:
A combination that you will seldom come across. Pronounce like English oy in toy. [ɔi]

hoi (hi)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ou
docs.text:
Same as au [au]

zout (salt)
vrouw (woman)
koud (cold)
nou (now)
stout (bad, naughty)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
This sound is something between ou and eu [ay]

zuid (south)
bruin (brown)
fluiten (to whistle)
buiten (outside)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: Ooi, aai, and oei
docs.text:
The letter i at the end is pronounced like English y in yes.

This sound is something between ou and eu [ay]

[aai] 

draai-en (to turn)
aai-en (to stroke)
maai-en (to mow)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

[oei] 

groei-en (to grow)
roei-en (to row)
ver-moeid (tired)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

[ooi] 

gooi-en (to throw)
mooi (beautiful)
ver-strooid (forgetful)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

docs.title: Ieu(w) and eeu(w)
docs.text:
These combinations are always followed by the consonant w.

Ieuw is pronounced as English ee followed by an English w and eeuw as English ay followed by w.

[eeu] 

leeu-wen (lions)
geeu-wen (to yawn)

Your browser does not support the audio element.

[Ieu] 

ver-nieu-wen (to renew)
kieu-wen (gills of a fish)

Your browser does not support the audio element.
